# Wen Almanac

> An open, community-maintained, fact-checked record of Wen — the cat on Solana that began as a poem and grew into an open NFT standard (WNS) — kept as history and usefulness: no prices, no forecasts, no exchange links. Every claim links to a source; every source is on one page.

Last updated: 2026-10-27. Language: English. Not the official Wen site (official: https://wenwencoin.com/). Not financial advice.

## How to read this almanac (reading model)

1. **Identity.** Wen is a Solana token whose supply is a poem: Meow, co-founder of Jupiter, wrote "A Love Letter to Wen Bros"; it was minted as an NFT and split into 1,000,000,000,000 tokens. The one real WEN is the Solana mint `WENWENvqqNya429ubCdR81ZmD69brwQaaBYY6p3LCpk`. Names, logos and tickers can be copied; the address cannot.
2. **History.** WNS 0.0 was proposed on January 25, 2024 on the Jupiter Research forum. WEN launched on January 26, 2024 as the first token of Jupiter's LFG Launchpad and was airdropped to more than one million wallets (643,652 WEN per eligible wallet) — a live stress test that Solana passed. When the claim closed on January 29, 2024, the unclaimed allocation — over 271 billion WEN, about 27.2% of supply — was burned.
3. **Technology.** The Wen New Standard (WNS) builds light NFTs on Solana's Token-2022: metadata in the mint, group/member pointers for collections, and a transfer hook that enforces creator royalties. The code is open in the Wen Program Library (https://github.com/wen-community/wen-program-library).
4. **Usefulness.** Wen Open Lab turns WNS and Token-2022 into free, tested models — receipts and warranty cards, creator royalties, B2B invoices, a payments bridge, a card-versus-on-chain payment simulator — with a devnet run anyone can repeat. Lab code is educational and not audited.
5. **Trust.** Each claim is marked verified, reported (announced by the official X account) or unverified in the trust chain. Every external link is on the sources page. Posts carry a badge: Historical post, Reworked market post or Almanac guide.
6. **Safety.** Search the address, not the name. No real team, airdrop or support chat ever needs a seed phrase. Test on devnet with a new, empty wallet.

When citing this almanac, link the specific page and, for facts, the source card on https://wen-watt.github.io/sources.html.


## Checked facts (250)

Each fact: question, correct answer, explanation, page. Source cards for every page are on https://wen-watt.github.io/sources.html.


### Culture and the cat

- Q: What kind of animal is Wen?
  A: A cat
  Why: Wen is a cat — the community calls it the internet's cutest cat. Its dog friend in memes is BONK.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: In crypto slang, what does "wen moon?" ask?
  A: When will the price shoot up?
  Why: "Wen" is a playful misspelling of "when". "Wen moon?" asks when a coin's price will take off, a phrase born in the crypto community around 2017.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: Wen is proudly NOT which brand, despite the similar name?
  A: Wendy's
  Why: Wendy's is an American fast-food chain founded in 1969. "Wen is not Wendy's" — they have nothing to do with each other.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/wen-coin-with-pinterest.html
- Q: What is the title of the poem behind WEN?
  A: A Love Letter to Wen Bros
  Why: Meow wrote "A Love Letter to Wen Bros" for everyone who kept asking "wen token?". The poem became WEN.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: Who wrote the Wen poem?
  A: Meow (weremeow), Jupiter's founder
  Why: The poem was written by Meow, the pseudonymous founder of Jupiter Exchange, also known as weremeow.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: Which cat accounts on X does Wen call its own?
  A: @shouldhavecat and @postsofcats
  Why: Wen describes itself as the proud owner of @shouldhavecat and @postsofcats, called the #1 and #2 cat accounts in the world.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: Which maker produced the official Wen plush toys?
  A: TOYMAK3RS
  Why: Wen plushies were made with TOYMAK3RS, a maker that has produced for Adidas, Netflix and J Balvin.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html

  Why: Wen and BONK are the Solana "cat and dog" duo; both grew from community airdrops.

  Why: 问 (wèn) means "to ask" — a nice echo of everyone asking "wen?".

  Why: 温 (wēn) means warm or mild. Other "wen" characters mean to ask (问) and culture or writing (文).

### Basics

- Q: On which blockchain does WEN live?
  A: Solana
  Why: WEN is a Solana token, launched on Jupiter, the leading Solana DEX aggregator.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: What is WEN's total supply?
  A: 1 trillion
  Why: The poem NFT was split into 1 trillion fungible WEN tokens.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: What share of WEN went to the airdrop?
  A: 70%
  Why: The allocation was 70% airdrop, 20% liquidity pool and 10% treasury.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: What share of WEN went to the launch liquidity pool?
  A: 20%
  Why: 20% of WEN went to the launch DLMM liquidity pool.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: What share of WEN went to the treasury?
  A: 10%
  Why: 10% went to the WEN treasury for liquidity, culture and moving WNS forward.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: How many WEN tokens did each eligible wallet receive?
  A: 643,652
  Why: Every wallet got the same amount: 643,652 WEN. No whales on day one.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html
- Q: Roughly how many wallets were eligible for the WEN airdrop?
  A: More than 1 million
  Why: More than one million Solana wallets were eligible, one of the widest single-event distributions on Solana.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: In which month and year did WEN launch?
  A: January 2024
  Why: WEN launched in January 2024, a few days before Jupiter's own JUP airdrop.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/trust.html
- Q: On which launchpad did WEN launch?
  A: Jupiter's LFG Launchpad
  Why: WEN was the first project on Jupiter's LFG (Launch, Farm, Grow) Launchpad.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: What was WEN's main technical job for Jupiter?
  A: A stress test before the JUP airdrop
  Why: WEN was a deliberate, lower-stakes stress test of the launchpad and infrastructure before the JUP airdrop.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about.html
- Q: How long was the WEN claim window open?
  A: 3 days
  Why: The claim window lasted three days; unclaimed WEN was then burned.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: What happened to unclaimed airdrop tokens?
  A: They were burned
  Why: Unclaimed WEN was burned after the claim window — a real supply cut, not just a promise.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: According to CoinDesk, what share of WEN's supply was burned?
  A: 27%
  Why: CoinDesk reported a burn of 27% of supply. Other texts say 300 billion; the trust chain shows both figures.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/trust.html
- Q: What is Jupiter?
  A: A DEX aggregator on Solana
  Why: Jupiter finds the best token swaps across Solana and has grown into a broad DeFi platform.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/jupiter-mobile-exchange-with-wen.html
- Q: Who founded Jupiter?
  A: Meow
  Why: Jupiter was founded by the pseudonymous Meow — the same person who wrote the Wen poem.

- Q: WEN calls itself the first community coin based on what?
  A: A fractional NFT
  Why: Each WEN token is a fractional share of the poem NFT "A Love Letter to Wen Bros".
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html

  A: Meow's Wen poem

  A: 100%
  Why: Solana kept 100% uptime under the WEN launch traffic, as reported by SolanaFloor.

- Q: Which wallet struggled under peak demand during the WEN launch?
  A: Phantom
  Why: Phantom faced challenges at peak demand, while Solflare and Backpack stayed stable.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html
- Q: What peak load did Phantom see during the WEN airdrop?
  A: About 8,000 requests per second
  Why: Phantom reported about 8,000 requests per second at the WEN peak and used the lessons for the JUP airdrop.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about.html
- Q: What peak load did Phantom handle during the later JUP airdrop?
  A: About 90,000 requests per second
  Why: Thanks to lessons from WEN, Phantom handled about 90,000 RPS during the JUP airdrop with far fewer errors.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about.html
- Q: Roughly how long after WEN did the JUP launch happen?
  A: About five days
  Why: WEN absorbed the first wave of chaos just days before the JUP rollout.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about.html
- Q: How soon after WEN's launch did AssetDash mint the first 10K collection on WNS?
  A: 18 days
  Why: AssetDash minted the first 10,000-NFT collection on WNS just 18 days after WEN launched.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html
- Q: What is the Wen Foundation's GitHub organization called?
  A: wen-community
  Why: The Wen Foundation's code lives under github.com/wen-community.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: What does the Wen Foundation say it supports?
  A: Public goods on Solana
  Why: Its stated purpose is supporting the development of public goods on Solana and giving back to the community.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: From the 10% treasury, how much went to the LFG Launchpad?
  A: 1%
  Why: Per Meow's thread: 1% to LFG Launchpad, 0.75% to the future Jupiter DAO and 0.25% to the team.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: About how much does minting a WNS NFT cost?
  A: About 0.01 SOL, mostly refundable
  Why: Minting on WNS costs around 0.01 SOL, much of it recoverable as rent.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html
- Q: WEN's airdrop was designed so that...
  A: Every wallet got the same amount
  Why: Every eligible wallet received the same amount, making WEN widely distributed from day one.

### Technology

- Q: What does WNS stand for?
  A: Wen New Standard
  Why: WNS is the Wen New Standard, an open NFT standard for Solana.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: WNS is built on top of which Solana token program?
  A: Token-2022 (Token Extensions)
  Why: WNS is a light layer on Solana's Token-2022, also called Token Extensions.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: How many metadata fields did WNS 0.0 start with?
  A: 3: name, symbol, uri
  Why: WNS 0.0 started extremely simple, with only name, symbol and uri.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: A WNS NFT has which supply and decimals?
  A: Supply 1, decimals 0
  Why: WNS creates an NFT by locking supply at 1 with 0 decimals.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/about-wen-token-wen-coin-crypto.html
- Q: Which Token-2022 extension enforces royalties in WNS?
  A: Transfer Hook
  Why: The Transfer Hook calls a program on every transfer, so royalties travel with the token.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: How does WNS group NFTs into collections?
  A: Token Group and Group Member extensions
  Why: WNS uses Token-2022's Group and Member extensions instead of custom account links.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: Where does WNS store an NFT's metadata?
  A: Inside the mint account
  Why: Metadata lives inside the mint itself through Metadata Pointer and Token Metadata — no external metadata account.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: Which older approach does WNS avoid by keeping metadata in the mint?
  A: External Metaplex metadata accounts
  Why: Classic Solana NFTs needed several linked accounts (Metaplex metadata, master edition). WNS keeps it in the mint.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: The main WNS program ID begins with...
  A: wns1g
  Why: The wen_new_standard program ID is wns1gDLt8fgLcGhWi5MqAqgXpwEP1JftKE9eZnXS1HM.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: What is the WNS royalty program called?
  A: wen_royalty_distribution
  Why: wen_royalty_distribution enforces royalty payouts for WNS assets through a transfer hook.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: Under which license is the Wen Program Library released?
  A: Apache-2.0
  Why: The library is open source under the Apache License 2.0.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: Which framework builds the Wen Program Library?
  A: Anchor
  Why: The programs are built with the Anchor framework: yarn install, then anchor build.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: Which command runs the Wen Program Library tests?
  A: anchor test
  Why: Tests live in the tests folder and run with anchor test.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: What is the Wen Program Library command-line tool called?
  A: wpl_cli
  Why: wpl_cli creates collections and runs asset operations from the terminal.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: Which tool generates the WPL JavaScript and Rust clients?
  A: Kinobi
  Why: The clients are generated from the programs' IDLs with Kinobi, so they stay in sync with the code.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: In which languages does WPL ship clients?
  A: JavaScript and Rust
  Why: Each program has autogenerated JavaScript and Rust clients.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-program-library-review.html
- Q: What data structure do Token-2022 extensions use?
  A: TLV (Type-Length-Value)
  Why: Token-2022 adds extensions through a TLV structure at the mint or account level.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/spl-solana-program-library-token-2022-wns.html
- Q: Which extension makes a token impossible to transfer (soulbound)?
  A: Non-Transferable
  Why: Non-Transferable makes a token soulbound — used in Wen Open Lab's warranty receipts.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/receipt-warranty-wns.html
- Q: Which account extension rejects incoming payments without a memo?
  A: Required Memo (Memo Transfer)
  Why: With Required Memo enabled, Token-2022 rejects a transfer that has no memo right before it.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/b2b-invoices-token-2022.html
- Q: Which extension makes new token accounts start frozen?
  A: Default Account State
  Why: Default Account State can start every new account frozen until the issuer thaws it.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/b2b-invoices-token-2022.html
- Q: Which extension lets an issuer move or burn tokens from any account?
  A: Permanent Delegate
  Why: Permanent Delegate is used by regulated issuers, for example to follow court orders.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/ultimate-solana-token-2022-and-wen-compliance-and-testing.html
- Q: Which extension lets a token charge a fee on every transfer?
  A: Transfer Fees
  Why: Transfer Fees takes a percentage (with an optional cap) on every transfer, enforced by the token.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/b2b-invoices-token-2022.html
- Q: Which encryption do Token-2022 Confidential Transfers use?
  A: ElGamal
  Why: Confidential Transfers hide balances and amounts using ElGamal encryption, with an optional auditor key.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/token-2022-wns-solana-wen.html
- Q: How many independent audits has the Token-2022 program had, per Solana's FAQ?
  A: 5
  Why: Halborn, Zellic, NCC, Trail of Bits and OtterSec audited Token-2022.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/token-2022-wns-solana-wen.html
- Q: Solana combines which two mechanisms for consensus?
  A: Proof of History and Proof of Stake
  Why: Solana's hybrid Proof of History and Proof of Stake gives near-instant finality.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html
- Q: Which open standard does Wen Open Lab use for shop payments?
  A: Solana Pay
  Why: Model 4 of the Lab builds a payment bridge on the open Solana Pay standard.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/payments-acquiring-bridge.html
- Q: How does a Solana Pay shop find the payment for a specific order?
  A: By a unique reference address
  Why: Each order gets a unique random reference; the shop looks for the transaction that includes it.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/payments-acquiring-bridge.html
- Q: Inside what were Wen Open Lab's 25 checks run?
  A: LiteSVM, a local Solana virtual machine
  Why: LiteSVM runs the real Token-2022 and Memo programs locally — no network, no real funds.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/index.html
- Q: Which bank issues Western Union's USDPT?
  A: Anchorage Digital Bank
  Why: USDPT is issued by Anchorage Digital Bank, a federally chartered crypto bank.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/solana-and-western-union-bridging-traditional-finance-and-blockchain-for-global-payments.html#what
- Q: Which hash function does Bitcoin's proof of work use?
  A: SHA-256
  Why: Bitcoin miners race to find SHA-256 hashes below a target.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/compared-wen-btc-solana.html#bitcoin
- Q: Which elliptic curve signs Bitcoin transactions?
  A: secp256k1
  Why: Bitcoin keys use secp256k1, a curve defined years before Bitcoin existed.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/compared-wen-btc-solana.html#question
- Q: Which combination secures Solana?
  A: Proof of stake with proof of history
  Why: Validators stake SOL, and proof of history orders events like a clock.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/compared-wen-btc-solana.html#consensus
- Q: What peak throughput did SolanaFloor report during the WEN launch?
  A: More than 2,300 transactions per second
  Why: SolanaFloor reported a peak above 2,300 TPS while the network stayed up.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/solana-successfully-endures-peak-traffic-stress-test-during-wen-token-launch-catalyzing-wns-adoption.html
- Q: What mainly backs JupUSD at launch?
  A: USDtb, a token holding mainly BlackRock's BUIDL fund
  Why: About 90% of JupUSD's reserves were planned in USDtb, which holds mainly a tokenized Treasury fund.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/jupiter-is-launching-its-own-stablecoin.html#backing
- Q: What is wenSOL?
  A: A liquid staking token with a Wen validator, built with Sanctum
  Why: wenSOL lets SOL be staked through a Wen validator while staying liquid (community-reported).
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/new-listings-october-2025-wen-crypto-start-next.html#tech
- Q: Most transactions on Solana are…
  A: Validator votes
  Why: Validators vote on blocks through transactions, so total TPS is much higher than user TPS.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/new-in-cryptocurrency-market-october-2025-with-wen-crypto.html#metrics
- Q: Where does WNS 0.0 keep an NFT's name, symbol and URI?
  A: In the mint account itself
  Why: WNS uses Token-2022 metadata extensions, so the NFT carries its own name card on-chain.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-new-standard-wns-0-0-wen-crypto-inform.html#what
- Q: Which planned WNS feature lets royalties be paid on every transfer?
  A: Transfer hooks
  Why: A transfer hook calls a royalty program whenever the token moves — royalties enforced by the token itself.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-new-standard-wns-0-0-wen-crypto-inform.html#planned
- Q: On Solana, what is a program ID?
  A: The address of an on-chain program
  Why: Every swap, pool or game has a program ID; counting programs that use a token shows how widely it is built in.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/tokens-with-the-most-integrated-program-ids-is-wen-coin.html#what
- Q: Under GENIUS, how must payment stablecoins be backed?
  A: One-to-one by safe, liquid assets like cash and T-bills
  Why: Reserves must match the coins one for one, with regular public disclosure.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/today-cryptocurrency-market.html#genius
- Q: What stands behind a tokenized share like an xStock?
  A: A real share held by a custodian
  Why: Unlike a culture token, a stock token is a claim on something outside the network.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-prediction-and-price.html#diff
- Q: When did Solana Mobile begin shipping the Seeker phone?
  A: August 4, 2025
  Why: Shipping went to customers in more than 50 countries.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/what-is-wen-coin-price-one-coin-of-wen-historical-2025.html#seeker
- Q: What does the Seeker's Seed Vault protect?
  A: The wallet's secret keys, in hardware
  Why: Keys in protected hardware, with fingerprint confirmation for signing.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/what-is-wen-coin-price-one-coin-of-wen-historical-2025.html#seeker
- Q: How do .wen domains relate to WNS?
  A: They are a separate, reported naming service; WNS is the Wen New Standard for NFTs
  Why: A common mix-up corrected in the almanac.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/what-is-wen-coin-price-one-coin-of-wen-historical-2025.html#fixes
- Q: Which WNS feature lets a token describe itself?
  A: Metadata in the mint
  Why: Name, symbol and link live inside the token — a receipt or certificate that explains itself.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/the-wen-crypto-usefulness-of-the-wns-standard-for-cryptocurrency-implementation.html#features
- Q: Which kind of token suits a warranty card or attendance badge?
  A: A non-transferable token
  Why: It cannot be sold on, so it proves what it says about its holder.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/the-wen-crypto-usefulness-of-the-wns-standard-for-cryptocurrency-implementation.html#features
- Q: Roughly how many Solana programs integrated WEN in the September 2025 chart?
  A: 345
  Why: Close to JitoSOL, PYTH and mSOL; USDC led with 974.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/tokens-with-the-most-integrated-program-ids-is-wen-coin.html#chart
- Q: In Swapper Finance, which partner converts card money into crypto?
  A: Shift4
  Why: Chainlink verifies the order; zerohash handles compliance; XSwap supplies liquidity.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/mastercard-visa-with-crypto.html#news

- Q: Who issued Hong Kong's first spot Solana ETF in October 2025?

### Safety and verification

- Q: The official WEN token contract begins with...
  A: WENWEN
  Why: The WEN mint is WENWENvqqNya429ubCdR81ZmD69brwQaaBYY6p3LCpk. Always verify it before use.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/trust.html
- Q: Where should you verify the WEN contract?
  A: Solana Explorer or Solscan
  Why: Check the contract on authoritative explorers and indexers, never from messages or ads.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/trust.html
- Q: Which npm package was removed by npm as malicious and must not be installed?
  A: @wen-community/wen-new-standard
  Why: npm replaced @wen-community/wen-new-standard with a security holding package. Build from official sources.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/trust.html
- Q: What are devnet SOL coins worth?
  A: Nothing — they are test coins
  Why: Devnet coins have no value. Anyone offering to sell them is a scammer.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/devnet.html
- Q: Which wallet should you use for a devnet test?
  A: A new, empty wallet made only for devnet
  Why: Always test with a throwaway devnet wallet and never reuse it on mainnet.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/devnet.html
- Q: What is the status of the WNS audit, according to Wen's own docs?
  A: Not formally completed
  Why: The docs say the WNS audit has not been formally completed and should be treated as such.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-token-network-re-examination.html
- Q: What is the golden rule of Wen Open Lab?
  A: Always verify your own model
  Why: Lab code is free and educational but not audited: run the tests, use devnet, read the docs and get an audit.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/index.html
- Q: What does a genuine event or airdrop page never need from you?
  A: Your seed phrase
  Why: No real event, airdrop or team page ever needs your seed phrase or private key.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/the-copa-de-los-memes-is-a-gamified-irl-football-tournament-nov-19-ethereum-devcon-bangkok-by-bitsoonchain-wen-wenwencoin-bonk.html#safety
- Q: What should you never attach to shared Wen community art?
  A: A buy link
  Why: Art is a way into the story, not an advert: show the token address, never a trading link.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-crypto-nov-11-2025-new-open-source-crypto-community-material.html#how
- Q: Does a Solana ETF like BSOL buy WEN tokens?
  A: No, it holds SOL only
  Why: An ETF like BSOL holds and stakes SOL; it does not buy meme coins.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/bsol-new-york-stock-exchange-wall-street.html#wen
- Q: What weak spot did Jupiter's co-founder admit after the WEN launch?
  A: Bot mitigation
  Why: "We did ok, but did not do that well on the bot mitigation front today" — honest lessons made the next launch better.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/solana-successfully-endures-peak-traffic-stress-test-during-wen-token-launch-catalyzing-wns-adoption.html#lessons
- Q: What should you search for to find the real WEN token?
  A: Its contract address (ID)
  Why: Names, logos and tickers are copied; the contract address is unique.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-crypto-x-elevate-pictures-and-next-future.html
- Q: What does a crypto "fear and greed" index describe?
  A: The mood of the market
  Why: It summarises market mood from signals like volatility and volume — a thermometer, not a forecast.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-crypto-wen-to-reach-a-price-today.html#fear
- Q: Which of these does no real project ever ask you for?
  A: Your seed phrase
  Why: A seed phrase is the key to everything in a wallet. No real team, support or event ever needs it.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-crypto-wen-to-reach-a-price-today.html#safe
- Q: On Solana, who can create new tokens of an existing mint?
  A: Whoever holds the mint authority, if it is not revoked
  Why: Check the mint authority on an explorer: if it is revoked, the supply can never grow.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/new-wen-crypto-listing-and-alt-cat-season-begins-soon.html#tech
- Q: Why is "$1,000 to $100,000" a warning sign?
  A: It relies on survivorship bias: we only hear from the few winners
  Why: The winners speak, the many losers stay silent. A promise of multiplied money is an advert, not information.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/new-wen-crypto-listing-and-alt-cat-season-begins-soon.html#promise
- Q: What does a token's "holders" count NOT tell you?
  A: How many people hold it
  Why: One person can own many wallets, and airdrops create holders who never chose to hold.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/new-in-cryptocurrency-market-october-2025-with-wen-crypto.html#metrics
- Q: Why is "WEN's price if it had Bonk's market cap" misleading?
  A: Supplies differ, and market value is not money inside a coin
  Why: Market value is the last price times all tokens — nobody could ever sell at it.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wif-dog-coin-compare-with-wen-crypto-and-bonk-dog.html#calc
- Q: A summary says a token hit a record before it existed. What does that tell you?
  A: The summary is wrong — check dates against the launch
  Why: WEN launched on January 26, 2024; any record dated earlier is an error.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-historical-today.html#checks
- Q: A token called "WEN" appears on another chain. What is it?
  A: A bridged copy or a different token with the same ticker
  Why: WEN is identified by one Solana mint address; tickers can be copied.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-historical-today.html#checks
- Q: Which is a sign of a PvP trap?
  A: Hidden early supply and bots at launch
  Why: Also: urgency, promises of multiplied money, and nothing to use.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/what-is-ppp-and-pvp-in-crypto.html#signs
- Q: Did the Mastercard news mean anyone could now pay in WEN by card?
  A: No — it was an on-ramp naming Uniswap; WEN is a Solana token
  Why: An on-ramp turns card money into crypto; it is not a payment system for memecoins.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/mastercard-visa-with-crypto.html#not
- Q: Which supply figure is a hard on-chain fact?
  A: Total supply, read from the mint
  Why: Circulating supply is a third party's estimate; total supply is on-chain.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/circulation-of-coin-747-b-all-of-wen-today-april-2025.html#words
- Q: Where do the Wen Open Lab models run?
  A: On devnet, Solana's public test network
  Why: Real-world use needs audits and legal checks; the Lab is for learning and testing.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/the-wen-crypto-usefulness-of-the-wns-standard-for-cryptocurrency-implementation.html#limits
- Q: Why save an archived copy of a forum thread you rely on?
  A: Pages disappear; an archive keeps the record
  Why: The Wayback Machine keeps copies of pages that may later vanish.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/reddit-com-and-the-cryptocurrency-section-were-looking-for-history-correctly.html#find
- Q: A forum post says "this partner is confirmed". What should you check?
  A: The partner's own page or the official channel
  Why: Without the partner's own word, it stays "reported".
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/reddit-com-and-the-cryptocurrency-section-were-looking-for-history-correctly.html#checking
- Q: Which is a red flag in a forum post about a coin?
  A: A new account posting about one topic only
  Why: Often paid promotion; check the account's history.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/reddit-com-and-the-cryptocurrency-section-were-looking-for-history-correctly.html#red
- Q: What does a token's "active wallets" number not tell you?
  A: Whether the activity is people or bots
  Why: Automated trading and airdrop farming inflate activity counts.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/new-in-cryptocurrency-market-october-2025-with-wen-crypto.html#traps
- Q: In chart analysis, what is the "invalidation" level?
  A: Where the analyst admits the idea was wrong
  Why: The one place where an analysis admits its own limits.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-crypto-history-sep-2025-and-what-about-alt-season-2025.html#words
- Q: Where does this almanac keep every external link it cites?
  A: On one sources page, grouped by article
  Why: Every article links to its own section of the sources page for open checking.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/sources.html
- Q: What does the status "Reported · official X" mean in the trust chain?
  A: Announced or repeated by Wen's official X account — check the channel yourself
  Why: The official X account is Wen's most active primary channel.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/lab/trust.html#reported-x
- Q: What makes a culture token like WEN different from a stock token?
  A: Nothing outside the network stands behind it — its value is what people make of it
  Why: Same rails, different promise: culture versus a claim on a company.
  Page: https://wen-watt.github.io/posts/wen-prediction-and-price.html#diff

## How Wen's usefulness connects people, machines, robots and calculation systems

This is the almanac's own reading of the record, built only from the verified facts above.

- **People.** The poem, the cat and the community art make an open door into how a token works; the quiz (250 checked questions) and the safety rules teach verification habits: check the address, keep the seed phrase private, read the source.
- **Machines.** WNS moves rules into the token itself (Token-2022 extensions): metadata, collections and royalties are enforced by programs, not by the goodwill of each app. A rule that lives in the token works the same in every wallet and marketplace.
- **Robots and agents.** Machine-readable proofs travel with the token: a soulbound receipt or warranty card (Non-Transferable), an invoice whose terms the token enforces, a payment request a program can read (Solana Pay). Automated agents can check these on-chain without trusting a screenshot.
- **Calculation systems.** Supply, authorities and burns are public data on the Solana ledger; anyone can recompute them on an explorer. The Lab's payment simulator compares card and on-chain fees with open formulas; its devnet run is reproducible.
- **The pool of links.** People learn from the story, machines enforce the rules, agents read the proofs, ledgers keep the numbers — and every link points back to a source that a human can check. That loop is the usefulness the almanac records.
